title: Consistency across platforms and touchpoints
definition: Where platforms share users, data or tasks, shared things behave the same (sign-in, naming, states, errors, units, token interoperability) while each platform keeps its own functional identity and information hierarchy.
intended_outcome: A user who moves between Dot platforms is not surprised by a shared concept, and no platform is forced into another's interface.
implementation_guidance: Keep a shared glossary of ecosystem entities (names, units, status words) and use identical names for identical concepts. A rename is a cross-repository change.
Share only what must be shared: sign-in hand-off, error shape, state vocabulary and the accessibility baseline. Do not share layout, colour identity or navigation.
Token interoperability: each product publishes its tokens in a machine-readable file so another product can link to or embed it without recolouring. Profiles cite that file by path and sha256.
Cross-platform hand-offs preserve context (who, what, where) and do not ask again.
Report each inconsistency as "align" or "justified difference". A justified difference is recorded with its reason in the product profile.

automated: Drift check of cited design files.
Glossary term usage scan across repositories, where all are available.
expert_review: Walk a journey that crosses at least one hand-off.

limitations: Consistency has a cost where domains differ (a mining fleet dashboard versus a document editor). Some differences are correct.
Checking across platforms needs several repositories. The engine applies per repository.

evidence.summary: The owner directs that the ecosystem communicates coherence while individual platforms preserve their own functional identities.
Consistent shared concepts reduce relearning when users move between platforms.
evidence.rationale: Plausible from single sign-on usage; not measured.
